mentions.heading: Climate change-driven severe weather may disrupt production and demand
mentions.risk_name: Severe weather disruption from climate change
mentions.detail: Storms, droughts, wildfires could disrupt GM plants, supplier production and logistics, dealer operations and customer demand
mentions.quote: In addition, increased intensity, frequency, or duration of storms, droughts, wildfires, or other severe weather events as a result of climate change may disrupt our production and the production, logistics, cost, and procurement of products from our suppliers, timely delivery of vehicles to customers and operations of our dealers, and could negatively impact working conditions at our plants and those of our suppliers and dealers.

mentions.heading: Our business is highly dependent upon global automobile market sales volume, which can be volatile
mentions.risk_name: Auto sales volume volatility with fixed costs
mentions.detail: High fixed structural costs magnify small sales declines; drivers include used vehicle prices, financing, rates, fuel costs
mentions.quote: Because we have a high proportion of relatively fixed structural costs, small changes in sales volume can have a disproportionately large effect on our profitability.

mentions.heading: Inflationary pressures and high prices and uncertain availability of commodities and inputs
mentions.risk_name: Commodity and semiconductor input cost inflation
mentions.detail: Steel, precious and non-ferrous metals, semiconductors raise production costs; may not pass on to customers
mentions.quote: Increases in prices, including as a result of inflation and rising interest rates, for commodities, raw materials, energy, or other inputs that we and our suppliers use in manufacturing products, systems, components, and parts, such as steel, precious metals, non-ferrous metals, critical minerals, or other similar raw materials, or electrical subcomponents, including transistors, diodes, and other semiconductors, or increases in logistics and related costs, have led and may continue to lead to higher production costs for parts, components, and vehicles.

mentions.heading: Cost and availability of critical EV battery materials
mentions.risk_name: EV battery critical mineral supply constraints
mentions.detail: Lithium, nickel, cobalt, rare earth metal cost or shortage could raise EV costs and impede EV strategy
mentions.quote: In addition, elevated cost, or reduced availability, of critical materials for our EV propulsion systems, including lithium, nickel, cobalt, and certain rare earth metals, may lead to higher production costs for our EVs and could impede our ability to successfully deliver on our EV strategy.

mentions.heading: Tariffs applicable to the automotive industry continue to evolve
mentions.detail: US tariffs on vehicles, parts, materials; USMCA review; mitigation via production changes won't fully offset; possible restructuring and impairments
mentions.quote: New or existing trade agreements, including the ongoing review of the U.S.-Mexico-Canada Agreement, may also impact the tariff rate applicable to goods imported by GM or our suppliers. Additionally, certain tariffs are subject to pending legal challenges.
